Boise State Broncos.strength: Stated explicitly and unusually strongly — he says the +1.7 win difference is one of the biggest he has ever produced in this exercise, that he double- and triple-checked the numbers, and that he would be willing to bet the total up to at least 8.5.
Boise State Broncos.headline: His model's biggest disagreement with the market, and he says he checked it twice.
Boise State Broncos.summary: Makinen's case is that the oddsmakers are giving too much credit to the strength of the new Pac-12 and that Boise State is the obvious favorite in it. He supports it with continuity — quarterback Maddux Madsen back as a senior, head coach Spencer Danielson in his fourth year — and with a schedule read that finds only one likely loss, the opener at Oregon. He states the size of his edge rather than implying it: a +1.7 win difference against the posted number, which he calls one of the biggest he has ever had, and adds that he would bet the total up to at least 8.5.
Boise State Broncos.over_argument: The market overrates the new Pac-12; Boise State is its obvious favorite, with a returning senior quarterback and a fourth-year head coach, and his ratings run against the schedule produce a 9.2-win projection against a total of 7.5.
Boise State Broncos.schedule_argument: He works through the slate and finds the opener at Oregon the only likely loss on it.

Boise State Broncos.ceiling_case: He says he would be willing to bet the number up to at least 8.5, which implies a nine-win view.
Boise State Broncos.futures_interaction: He calls Boise State the obvious favorite to take the newly formed Pac-12.

Fresno State Bulldogs.strength: Not stated as a strength rating.
Fresno State Bulldogs.headline: A first-year coach who did not need settling-in time, plus a returning-starter system angle.
Fresno State Bulldogs.summary: Makinen records that Fresno State exceeded his expectations in Matt Entz's first year, finishing 9-4 where he would have allowed a coach time to find his footing. Entz followed it with a recruiting class 247Sports graded as extremely improved. With 13 starters back the Bulldogs also qualify for one of his transition systems: of 141 teams over five years that brought back at least four more starters than the prior season, only 40 got worse, and the rest averaged a 15% winning-percentage gain — about +3.2 wins — with a 6.7% ATS rise.
Fresno State Bulldogs.over_argument: A coach who succeeded immediately, an improved recruiting class, 13 returning starters, and a documented system angle for teams adding starters year over year.
Fresno State Bulldogs.schedule_argument: He notes the move into the remade Pac-12 as context but does not work through the slate.
Fresno State Bulldogs.coaching_argument: Matt Entz exceeded expectations in year one at 9-4 and responded by improving the recruiting class.
Fresno State Bulldogs.roster_argument: Thirteen starters back, which qualifies Fresno State for his returning-starters transition system.

Florida Atlantic Owls.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he calls this a chance at FAU's best season since the Lane Kiffin days.
Florida Atlantic Owls.headline: Three separate transition systems all pointing up from a turnover-wrecked season.
Florida Atlantic Owls.summary: Makinen's case is regression-to-the-mean stacked three ways. Zach Kittley's first FAU team led the country in offensive plays and passing yards per game and also led it in giveaways. He records quarterback Caden Veltkamp back for his senior year after 3,600-plus passing yards, plus 11 other starters, and then lists three system angles the Owls qualify for: teams going .500 or better ATS despite a turnover margin of -0.8 or worse (only four of 18 regressed, average +1.4 wins); teams winning four or fewer games with that same turnover ratio since 2021 (only two of 21 regressed, average +2.3 wins); and teams adding at least four starters year over year (only 40 of 141 got worse).
Florida Atlantic Owls.over_argument: A year of system experience, a returning senior quarterback, 11 other returning starters, and three separate historical angles all pointing to improvement from a season wrecked by giveaways.
Florida Atlantic Owls.schedule_argument: He notes that a lot of American Conference teams face questions this season, which he treats as opening the door.
Florida Atlantic Owls.qb_argument: Caden Veltkamp returns for his senior year after throwing for over 3,600 yards.
Florida Atlantic Owls.coaching_argument: Second-year head coach Zach Kittley, whose first team he calls fun to watch, now has a year in the new system behind it.
Florida Atlantic Owls.roster_argument: Twelve returning starters in total, which triggers the added-starters transition angle.
Florida Atlantic Owls.ceiling_case: He frames the upside as FAU's best football year since the Lane Kiffin era.
Florida Atlantic Owls.risks: The giveaways are stated as the thing that has to change: the Owls led the nation in them.

Houston Cougars.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he calls it a big year for Fritz & Co.
Houston Cougars.headline: One of only two teams on his own Stability Score of 18, with Notre Dame the other.
Houston Cougars.summary: Makinen builds this on stability and recruiting. The move to the Big 12 has produced Houston's best five-year run of recruiting classes on record, and under Willie Fritz he says a new consistent standard is being set after nine regular-season wins and a Texas Bowl win over LSU. Quarterback Conner Weigman returns as a senior after a huge year, within 19 returning starters — one of only two teams with a Stability Score of 18 on his scale, alongside Notre Dame. He adds two supporting angles: teams returning 17-plus starters have gone 55.7% ATS in the first four weeks of the last five seasons, and teams adding four or more starters year over year improved in 101 of 141 cases.
Houston Cougars.over_argument: The highest tier of returning experience on his own stability scale, a returning senior quarterback, record recruiting since the Big 12 move, and momentum from a nine-win regular season and a bowl win over LSU.
Houston Cougars.qb_argument: Conner Weigman, the former Texas A&M transfer, had a huge year and is back for his senior season.
Houston Cougars.coaching_argument: Willie Fritz is establishing a new, consistent standard.
Houston Cougars.roster_argument: Nineteen starters back, a Stability Score of 18 — one of two nationally — plus the 17-plus-starters ATS angle for the first four weeks.
Houston Cougars.best_bet_interaction: He notes the 17-plus-starters group's 55.7% ATS record in the first four weeks, which is a side-market angle rather than a win-total one.

Illinois Fighting Illini.headline: A programme he says has turned a corner, with a Big Ten starter replacing a Big Ten starter.
Illinois Fighting Illini.summary: Makinen returns to a bet that won for him last season. His case is programme trajectory: Bret Bielema's best recruiting class on record, 19 wins over two seasons, and a rise from Big Ten recruiting bottom-feeder to a mid-level destination — which he reads as a corner turned rather than a spike. He grants the loss of Luke Altmyer but replaces him with another former Big Ten starter in Katin Houser from Michigan State, with 11 other starters in place. On the schedule he names Ohio State and Oregon and says it is hard to see the Illini as a likely loser in any other game.
Illinois Fighting Illini.over_argument: A programme on a sustained upward trajectory with recruiting to match, an experienced Big Ten replacement at quarterback, and a schedule with only two games he considers likely losses.

Kansas State Wildcats.strength: Not stated as a strength rating.
Kansas State Wildcats.headline: Five of six losses by six points or fewer, with a senior quarterback and a homecoming hire.
Kansas State Wildcats.summary: Makinen's case rests on close-game arithmetic and continuity through a coaching change. Chris Klieman retired citing personal health and family after a 6-6 season, but left reasonable starting experience behind, led by third-year starting quarterback Avery Johnson. Collin Klein takes over for his first head-coaching job after seven seasons in Manhattan as an offensive assistant and two as Texas A&M's coordinator; Makinen notes he played at KSU from 2008-12, has a tremendous bond with the programme, and that the hire drew a lot of optimism. The pivot is that five of last season's six losses came by six points or fewer. With no Texas Tech or BYU on the slate he gives Kansas State an outside shot at the Big 12 title game.
Kansas State Wildcats.over_argument: A 6-6 team that lost five games by six points or fewer, returning a senior third-year starting quarterback, under a first-time head coach with deep programme roots and a schedule that misses the conference's two strongest teams.
Kansas State Wildcats.schedule_argument: No Texas Tech and no BYU on the 2026 slate, which he says gives Kansas State an outside shot at a Big 12 title game berth.

Kansas State Wildcats.roster_argument: A reasonable amount of starting experience returning.

South Alabama Jaguars.headline: A recruiting class 31 places better than last year's, in a conference short of favorites.
South Alabama Jaguars.summary: Makinen opens by admitting he cannot always explain why a recruiting jump happens, then records the jump: in his third season, coming off 4-8, Major Applewhite secured his best recruit and transfer class, ranked 86th — 31 positions better than the prior year — with several Power Four transfers among the newcomers. Quarterback Bishop Davenport returns for his senior season after leading the team to 26.5 points per game. South Carolina Gamecocks.headline: A five-win drop he calls unexpected, with the stars back and two transition systems attached.
South Carolina Gamecocks.summary: Makinen treats last season's five-win regular-season decline as unexpected and partly bad luck: four losses by 10 points or fewer, all to teams ranked in the top 25 at the time. Key players stayed, quarterback LaNorris Sellers among them. He then attaches two system angles — teams returning nine or more offensive starters including the quarterback after winning 50% or less of their games average +2.7 wins, and of 43 teams that had losing seasons despite outscoring opponents, the 17 that brought back 13-plus starters including the quarterback improved by about 20% straight up (+3.4 wins) and went 56.5% ATS. He closes on schedule: a realistic shot at heading to Florida in October at 4-1 or better, with a win there giving real momentum.
South Carolina Gamecocks.over_argument: An unlucky 2025 with four narrow losses to ranked teams, the offensive star retained, and two historical systems both pointing to a multi-win rebound.

Syracuse Orange.headline: A 10-3 to 3-9 collapse he reads as a turnover-driven bounce-back candidate.
Syracuse Orange.summary: Makinen explains the 10-3 to 3-9 fall as the standard yo-yo — heavy losses from a successful team, compounded by turnovers — and then applies his nowhere-to-go-but-up system: since 2021, of 21 teams winning four or fewer games with a turnover ratio of -0.8 or worse, only two regressed, and the other 19 averaged +2.3 wins and a 15.3% straight-up improvement. He adds recruiting: Fran Brown, in his third season, landed the second-highest-rated class Syracuse has seen in 17 years despite the 3-9 record, which Makinen reads as evidence he is a strong salesman. With quarterback Steve Angeli back as a senior and the ACC looking down, he expects a rebound.
Syracuse Orange.over_argument: A turnover-wrecked four-win season that his system says almost always improves, plus a recruiting jump and a returning senior quarterback in a weak conference.

Syracuse Orange.risks: Turnovers, which he identifies as a major cause of the 2025 collapse.

Texas Longhorns.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he calls 11-1 realistic.
Texas Longhorns.headline: A late-season surge, the country's top recruiting, and a quarterback he says is ready.
Texas Longhorns.summary: Makinen frames 2025 as a season played under palpable pressure, noting Texas still won 10 games despite going 5-7-1 against the spread — which he reads as evidence of how highly the bookmakers rated them. The turn came at the end: three straight wins to close, Arch Manning exploding statistically, and 456 yards in the bowl win over Michigan. He adds a first-ever No. 1 recruiting class followed by a No. 3, and one transition system: of 33 teams since 2021 with nine or more returning offensive starters including the quarterback off a season under 45% ATS, only three got worse, with the rest averaging +2.0 wins and a 16.8% ATS gain. Two more wins would put Texas at 11-1, which he calls realistic.
Texas Longhorns.over_argument: Closing momentum with a quarterback who broke out over the final three games, elite recruiting in consecutive cycles, and a system angle for returning offensive starters off a poor ATS season.
Texas Longhorns.schedule_argument: Not worked through game by game, though the conference table records Texas with the toughest schedule in the country.
Texas Longhorns.qb_argument: Arch Manning exploded statistically over the final three games and he judges him 100% ready to fulfil his immense promise.
Texas Longhorns.coaching_argument: Steve Sarkisian's team won its final three games of 2025.
Texas Longhorns.roster_argument: Nine or more returning offensive starters including the quarterback, which triggers his transition system.
Texas Longhorns.ceiling_case: Two additional wins would put Texas at 11-1, which he calls realistic.
Texas Longhorns.best_bet_interaction: He cites the comparison group's 53% ATS record and 16.8% ATS improvement.

Texas A&M Aggies.strength: Not stated as a strength rating, though he calls this one of the most stable teams in the country.
Texas A&M Aggies.headline: Stability stacked three ways behind a returning quarterback and 17 other starters.
Texas A&M Aggies.summary: Makinen makes this his stability showcase. Mike Elko's third year follows a CFP appearance ended by Miami at home, and he expects last season's three-win growth to be a stepping stone to elite territory. Quarterback Marcel Reed returns as a junior alongside 17 other starters. Three angles are stacked: teams returning a starting quarterback for a second straight season improve by about 0.9 wins; adding the same head coach and offensive coordinator plus seven or more other offensive returnees lifts that to 1.3 wins and 53.3% ATS, with only 12 of 38 winning fewer games; and of 33 teams since 2021 with nine-plus returning offensive starters including the quarterback off a sub-45% ATS season, only three got worse. His summary is a very stable situation with a very talented roster and staff.
Texas A&M Aggies.over_argument: Continuity at head coach, coordinator and quarterback with 17 other starters back, three separate historical systems all pointing up, and a programme he expects to move into elite territory.
Texas A&M Aggies.qb_argument: Marcel Reed returns as a junior, and the returning-starter-at-quarterback angle is the base of his whole case.
Texas A&M Aggies.coaching_argument: Mike Elko in year three, with the same head coach and offensive coordinator as part of the stability angle.
Texas A&M Aggies.roster_argument: Seventeen other starters back, which he calls exclamation-worthy.

UCLA Bruins.headline: A coaching upgrade he calls obvious, with the quarterback retained and 18 new starters.
UCLA Bruins.summary: Makinen's case is a new-coach-plus-returning-quarterback system. Bob Chesney arrives from a James Madison CFP season to replace DeShaun Foster, who went 8-16 over two years. He records 2025 as a massive disappointment, particularly after landing Nico Iamaleava, who he says was vilified when the team struggled and praised during a shocking three-game Big Ten winning streak in October. Chesney gets Iamaleava back plus numerous Power Four transfers, amounting to 18 starting players filling spots. The system: over five years, 21 teams that won under 50% and then brought back their starting quarterback while hiring a new head coach and coordinators improved by 15.2% straight up (+2.1 wins) and 13.3% ATS, with only one getting worse. He counts six very winnable home games and calls the coaching upgrade obvious.
UCLA Bruins.over_argument: A returning starting quarterback combined with a new head coach and new coordinators — his strongest documented improvement system — plus heavy Power Four portal reinforcement and six winnable home games.
UCLA Bruins.schedule_argument: He counts six very winnable home games.

UCLA Bruins.roster_argument: Numerous Power Four transfers, amounting to about 18 starting players filling spots — a number he calls lofty in this era.

Virginia Tech Hokies.headline: A coaching upgrade plus 18 returning or added starters, in an ACC full of question marks.
Virginia Tech Hokies.summary: Makinen notes James Franklin's Penn State teams never met the fans' demands but says he has rarely been as effusive about an offseason, and that the excitement around Virginia Tech is palpable.
